topics.topic: Startup timing, phase alignment, and shared-versus-independent execution of lifecycle passes
questions: Does the backup look run once immediately when the process starts and then every 60 seconds, or does its first call occur only after the first 60-second interval?
When are the first calls made after process start, and do the session pass and backup look share one tick and phase or run on independent schedules?
Does `instance_lifecycle` call each module immediately when the process starts, or only after its first 60-second interval, and are the two schedules phase-aligned?

Are the session pass and backup look independent scheduled tasks, or are they serial calls on one 60-second loop; if serial, in which order, and may a long backup run delay later session passes or looks?

quotes:
The start and the running instance: `configuration` first, then the backup
probe and `store`, then the listeners at the release's addresses, serving
nothing until every check passed and having `store` remove a store this start
made new when a listener cannot be opened (A17 rule 2); the
owner-only start, which opens the owner interface alone (A17 rule 1, A18
rule 9); the two surfaces, the owner interface's listener opened first; the 60-second pass
of `owner_sessions` and the minute look of `backups` (A13 rule 2, A18 rule 1);
that a restart ends every owner session (A13 rule 2).
judgement.why: The first-call phase, alignment, serialization order and effect of long-running work are flow and scheduling-order questions owned by State 4, while State 3 already assigns both timers to `instance_lifecycle`.

topics.topic: Ownership and sharing of the two 60-second schedule constants
questions: Which module owns these two release values, and are they one shared constant or two independently named constants?
Which module owns each 60-second schedule value, and are they one shared constant or two independently owned constants?

quotes:
The typed constants of the data closure, the one home of each value the
generated code reads that is not a setting of the environment (SPEC_STANDARD
§6.10, §15.3.1; reopened 2026-11-11, replacing the former
release_declarations module): the
artifact types with their owner services, the first release's one row
(`estimate`, PresuPro) (A22); A09 rule 2's table of the services, their
operations and their highest classes; the store version and the store's
temporary-name suffix (A17 rule 5); the kept and temporary backup prefixes,
neither beginning with the other, the daily time, the minute look and the
retention of 30 × 24 hours (A18 rules 1, 4, 5); the import file's size limit
(A19 rule 4); the release's own version and its contract version, which
every audit entry names (M09) and a backup's record names (A18 rule 1); the
address each surface listens on, which the configuration does not name
(A17 rules 1, 2); the owner session's limits — 8 hours, 30 minutes, the 15
minutes and five refusals of the sign-in, the 10 minutes of a confirmation,
the 60 seconds of the pass (A13); the request id's 128 characters (A01 rule
1), the alias's 40 (A02 rule 4), the 32 bytes of a secret value and of a
configured secret (A13 rule 7, A17 rule 3). The list names groups; the data
closure names each constant, and every one is exported.

BACKUP_LOOK_SECONDS
BACKUP_RETENTION_HOURS
IMPORT_FILE_MAX_BYTES
RELEASE_VERSION

OWNER_INTERFACE_LISTEN_ADDRESS
SERVICE_API_LISTEN_ADDRESS
OWNER_SESSION_MAX_HOURS
OWNER_SESSION_IDLE_MINUTES
SIGN_IN_WINDOW_MINUTES
SIGN_IN_REFUSAL_LIMIT
SIGN_IN_LOCKOUT_MINUTES
CONFIRMATION_VALID_MINUTES
SESSION_PASS_SECONDS
judgement.why: `data_provider` owns both release values, and the distinct exported names `BACKUP_LOOK_SECONDS` and `SESSION_PASS_SECONDS` make them two independently named constants applied by `instance_lifecycle`.

topics.topic: Ownership of the mechanism that generates each 60-second lifecycle tick
questions: Which module owns the mechanism that waits for or emits each 60-second tick, given that `clock` hides the host clocks and exports only readings?
What module owns the wait/timer mechanism by which `instance_lifecycle` applies an interval, given that `clock` hides the host clocks but exports only readings?

quotes:
The start and the running instance: `configuration` first, then the backup
probe and `store`, then the listeners at the release's addresses, serving
nothing until every check passed and having `store` remove a store this start
made new when a listener cannot be opened (A17 rule 2); the
owner-only start, which opens the owner interface alone (A17 rule 1, A18
rule 9); the two surfaces, the owner interface's listener opened first; the 60-second pass
of `owner_sessions` and the minute look of `backups` (A13 rule 2, A18 rule 1);
that a restart ends every owner session (A13 rule 2).
The process's start sequence, its timers and the two listening surfaces.
judgement.why: `instance_lifecycle` owns and hides the timers that generate the calls; `clock` owns readings and is expressly forbidden from owning a schedule.

topics.topic: Ownership of time sampling, backup due decisions, and backup scheduling state
questions: Does `instance_lifecycle` read the clock and pass sampled readings to `owner_sessions` and `backups`, or do those modules depend on `clock` and read time when they execute?

Does `instance_lifecycle` merely invoke the two modules, or does it read `clock`, decide that a backup is due, and pass a time/date to `backups`; correspondingly, which module owns the remembered dates already run and the earlier-before-03:00 observation?

quotes:
A18: the daily run at 03:00 UTC while Registry runs with its tokens, from the
minute look and the dates the process remembers (rule 1); the copy, without
agent sessions, that `store` writes at the temporary path `backups` names
(rule 2), encrypted with the configured key, recording its
instant, release, last sequence number and key digest (rules 1, 3); the three
steps — removing temporary files, writing and checking the backup by
decrypting it and asking `store` to check the copy, deleting backups older
than 30 × 24 hours and unreadable ones (rule 4); the prefixes and the location
rules (rule 5), the probe file of A17 rule 2; the newest kept backup's instant
for the owner interface. No run in an owner-only start (rule 9).

A13 and M11, all runtime state: the sign-in with the owner credential, its
count of refusals over the last 15 minutes and the lockout, one answer whatever
was wrong (rules 3, 4); the session, its cookie rules and its limits — 8 hours,
30 minutes without a request, sign-out, restart — held as monotonic readings
(rule 2); the pass every 60 seconds that ends sessions by their limits, taking
the import lock and then each session's lock; each session's one lock, under
which its state-changing requests apply one at a time; the CSRF value (rule 5);
the pending confirmation — made when a step is shown, bound to the action, its
target, the revision or access version the step showed or that it showed none,
and the digest of its inputs; valid 10 minutes, used up by the first
submission that carries it, cleared by an expired one (rule 6). The uploaded
import file each session keeps in memory, replaced by the next upload — one of
the same bytes included — and dropped with the session or by an accepted
import (A16 rule 2), and the instance's one import lock, taken before any
session's lock.
What any check or pass decides.
judgement.why: `instance_lifecycle` invokes the passes but must not decide them; `backups` owns the minute look and remembered dates and knows `clock`, while `owner_sessions` owns its pass and monotonic session state and also knows `clock`.

topics.topic: Policy for lifecycle ticks missed during suspension or long-running work
questions: When suspension or a long-running call crosses one or more 60-second boundaries, are missed calls coalesced into one immediate call, replayed once per missed interval, or discarded with the cadence restarted?

quotes:
the 60 seconds of the session pass and of the minute
look are ones that `instance_lifecycle` applies, calling `owner_sessions` and
`backups` at those intervals.
judgement.why: Coalescing, replaying or discarding missed timer invocations is observable flow and scheduling behavior owned by State 4, not a State 3 module-ownership decision.

topics.topic: Whether backup polling cadence uses monotonic elapsed time or UTC wall-clock time
questions: Which `clock` capability measures the minute-look interval for backups? A13 explicitly makes the session-pass interval monotonic, but A18 does not say whether its polling cadence is driven by monotonic elapsed time or UTC wall-clock time.

quotes:
the 60 seconds of the session pass and of the minute
look are ones that `instance_lifecycle` applies, calling `owner_sessions` and
`backups` at those intervals.
judgement.why: State 3 assigns the backup-look schedule to `instance_lifecycle` but does not choose the timer's elapsed-time basis; that cadence behavior belongs to State 4 flows.
